why_local.text: You control the whole chain: the model, its exact version, the serving software and who can reach it. No outside service joins your attack surface.
No rate limits, no outages caused by someone else's demand, no surprise deprecations. A validated, pinned model behaves the same next month, which matters most for your always-on agents.
Prompts, documents and answers never leave your network. That is a simpler guarantee than any contract a provider can offer, and it matters for the regulated data you hold.
Open weights let you train on your own material or distill a faster model, locally, without handing data or weights to a provider.

blockers.guidance: Start with the honest cost comparison below and the smallest pilot; only buy hardware after the pilot proves value.
A security review packet (data flows, egress policy, threat model, model provenance and licenses, pinning and update process) is generated next to this file.

pilot_plan: Days 1-2: run the advisor, install only the recommended runtime and model, confirm outbound traffic is blocked (make egress-test).
Days 3-4: write 20-30 real questions your team asks (the golden set) and record today's answers and time spent.
Days 5-7: daily use by one or two people; log what worked and what did not.
Days 8-10: if documents matter, ingest one folder and test search with citations against the golden set.
Days 11-12: review the audit log, memory use and speed against the estimates here.
Days 13-14: decide go / adjust / stop, using the golden-set results and the cost comparison.

privacy.egress: Deny all outbound by default. Model downloads happen only in a separate `make pull` step. SearXNG may reach search engines (named exception).
privacy.encryption_at_rest: Full-disk encryption required (FileVault / LUKS / BitLocker); encrypted backups.
privacy.encryption_in_transit: TLS on the LAN via Caddy's local CA
privacy.remote_access: None by default; if needed, WireGuard/Tailscale only. Never port-forward.
privacy.acl_enforcement: Per-user and per-collection ACLs enforced in the database query (Postgres row-level security), not only in the UI.
privacy.compliance_note: Regulated data present. These controls support privacy obligations but do not by themselves make you compliant with HIPAA, PCI, GDPR or similar; review with your compliance advisor.

tco.verdict: On these estimates, a hosted open-weight model API would be cheaper than local by about $49,204 over three years. Local is recommended here for security, availability, privacy, not price. Note that the hosted options would send prompts and documents off-site, which this profile's regulated data makes a compliance question.
